title.en: Should Companies Adopt a Four-Day Week?
title.zh: 公司該實施每週工作四天嗎？

subtitle: 原創模擬題：學術討論題，談每週工作四天的利弊
task:
Your professor is teaching a class on business management. Write a post responding to the professor's question. In your response, express and support your opinion, and make a contribution to the discussion.

Dr. Lin: Several companies around the world have tested a four-day work week, in which employees work fewer days but receive the same salary. Do you think more companies should adopt this schedule? Why or why not?

Aiden: Yes. When people have three days to rest, they come back to work with more energy and make fewer mistakes. Happier workers are also less likely to quit.

Priya: I doubt it works for every business. Hospitals, restaurants and shops need staff every day, so a shorter week would just create scheduling problems for them.

Write at least 100 words.
taskZh: 企業管理課的教授提問：世界各地有些公司試行每週工作四天、薪水不變的制度。你認為應該有更多公司採用嗎？為什麼？Aiden 支持，認為員工休息充足、精力較好、失誤較少，也比較不會離職；Priya 懷疑它適合所有行業，因為醫院、餐廳和商店每天都需要人手。請寫一則貼文表態、提出理由，並對討論有新的貢獻。至少寫 100 字。
focus: 直接回答教授的問題並清楚表態
回應兩位同學的觀點，再提出新的理由或折衷方案
用具體的例子或理由支持看法，論點前後一致
用字精確、句型多樣、文法正確

en: I think more companies should try a four-day work week, but they should introduce it carefully. Aiden makes a strong point about energy and mistakes, and I believe the schedule could also help companies attract talented young workers. Many people my age care about free time as much as salary, so a shorter week would be a powerful advantage when hiring.

At the same time, Priya is correct that not every business can close one day a week. However, a four-day week does not have to mean that everyone takes the same day off. A restaurant, for example, could divide its staff into two teams with different days off, so it stays open seven days a week. Companies could test the idea for a few months before deciding whether to keep it.
zh: 我認為應該有更多公司嘗試每週工作四天，但要謹慎推行。Aiden 提到精力和失誤，這點很有說服力；我認為這種制度還能幫公司吸引有才華的年輕員工。很多和我同年紀的人重視休閒時間的程度不亞於薪水，所以縮短工作週在招募人才時會是很大的優勢。
同時，Priya 說得沒錯，並不是每種行業都能每週休息一天。不過，每週工作四天不代表所有人都要在同一天休假。例如，餐廳可以把員工分成休假日不同的兩組，這樣就能一週七天照常營業。公司可以先試行幾個月，再決定是否繼續。

patterns.pattern: I think … should …, but they should …
patterns.zh: 表態並加上執行的條件
patterns.example: I think more companies should try a four-day work week, but they should introduce it carefully.

patterns.pattern: … makes a strong point about …, and I believe …
patterns.zh: 肯定同學的觀點，再補充自己的想法
patterns.example: Aiden makes a strong point about energy and mistakes, and I believe the schedule could also help companies attract talented young workers.

patterns.pattern: …, so … would be a powerful advantage when …
patterns.example: Many people my age care about free time as much as salary, so a shorter week would be a powerful advantage when hiring.

patterns.pattern: At the same time, … is correct that …
patterns.zh: 轉折：承認另一位同學也有道理
patterns.example: At the same time, Priya is correct that not every business can close one day a week.

patterns.pattern: … does not have to mean that …
patterns.zh: 澄清誤解，提出不同的做法
patterns.example: However, a four-day week does not have to mean that everyone takes the same day off.
keys: does not have to mean that

parts: A restaurant could divide its staff into two teams.
It could stay open seven days a week.
combine.answer: A restaurant could divide its staff into two teams, so it could stay open seven days a week.

parts: Companies could test the idea for a few months.
Then they could decide whether to keep it.
combine.answer: Companies could test the idea for a few months before deciding whether to keep it.

paraphrase.sentence: Not every business can close one day a week.
answers: Some businesses cannot take a day off every week.
Closing one day a week is impossible for some companies.

paraphrase.sentence: Many people care about free time as much as salary.
answers: For many people, free time matters as much as pay.
Many workers value their free time as highly as their salary.
